message.content:
(1) Overall layout structure: MATCH. Both use a three-pane layout with a left navigation tree, a central file list, and a right-side details/preview area.
(2) Information architecture: MATCH. Both feature a file tree on the left, a sortable table (Name, Date, Type) in the center, and a selection summary/preview pane on the right.
(3) Color palette family: MATCH. Both utilize a clean light theme with white backgrounds, blue primary accents for buttons and links, and neutral grays for borders and text.
(4) Typography scale: MATCH. Both use a clear hierarchy with bold headers for panes, standard sans-serif fonts for the list items, and smaller meta-text for dates and sizes.
(5) Control geometry: DIFF. Image 2 includes additional columns ("Size", "Condition") in the main list and uses a more compact row height compared to the sparser layout of Image 1.
(6) Primary CTA placement: MATCH. In both interfaces, the primary "Recover" action is positioned as a prominent blue button in the bottom-right corner of the window.

VERDICT: STRUCTURALLY_EQUIVALENT. The re-implementation successfully captures the core spatial organization, functional zones, and visual language of the reference product despite minor differences in list density and column configuration.
